Updated read with SLOOS overlay:
- Policy: A 25 bp cut to 4.25–4.50% with “roughly balanced” risks and continued QT signals cautious, data‑dependent easing. Implementation via IOER at 4.4%, ON RRP at the floor, and standing facilities is consistent with a floor/corridor framework and avoids an outright loosening of financial conditions. One dissent (preferring no cut) underscores inflation‑persistence concerns.
- SLOOS credit backdrop: Banks report tight C&I standards and weaker loan demand among small and some middle‑market firms; CRE standards remain tight (with large banks unchanged in CLD and somewhat easier for multifamily); household credit remains tiered with tighter standards for subprime, while RRE and HELOC standards are broadly unchanged. Foreign banks’ C&I standards are unchanged with some pockets of stronger demand. Reasons cited include economic outlook, risk tolerance, capital/liquidity, and sector‑specific issues.
- Implications: With bank lending standards still restrictive and demand soft in credit‑sensitive segments, the growth impulse from a single 25 bp cut is likely moderated. That reinforces the Fed’s cautious, data‑dependent stance even as inflation continues to trend lower. Combined with financial‑stability vulnerabilities flagged in the FSR, this tilts the read slightly more cautious than a pure macro take.

Bottom line: Still cautiously positive on activity and disinflation progress, but SLOOS‑indicated credit headwinds warrant a small downgrade in tone versus a non‑credit read.
